RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-women panel is not evidence of bias. Panel composition reflects who is available and senior in that function; in many ministries women are heavily represented in HR and policy leadership. Mixed and single-sex panels both routinely select candidates of either sex. On its own, the number proves nothing, and raising it reads as an accusation you can't support — which damages your standing far more than it helps.

The real issues are substantive: your qualifications look strong on paper, but "leading international projects" may have been the decisive criterion, and you don't yet know how you scored.

Chase the written feedback — formally, in writing, citing any statutory deadline. Ask for scores against the published criteria. Judge the process on that, not the panel's sex.
